clues: This city in the east of Washington state lies by a river, near high hills. It sits west of the Rocky foothills, a short way south of the border with Canada.
High hills to the west wring most rain from the clouds first. So this city gets less than half the rain of the big coast city in its state.
In 1810 a trade post was set up here by men who came to trade. It was the first lasting town of men from Europe in all of Washington.
This city is known as the birthplace of Father's Day. Each year its folk mark the day for dads that first began here, long ago.
Each year this city hosts the world's largest game of three on three basketball. Teams come from far and wide to play in the big contest.
